Deployment Guide

Docker Deployment

Hydrozoa is container-first and ready for deployment with Docker.

  1. Build the Docker Image: 
    docker build -t hydrozoa:latest .
  2. Run the Container: 
    docker run -d \
  -p 3000:3000 \
  --env-file .env \
  --name hydrozoa-agent \
  hydrozoa:latest
  3. Verify Deployment: Check the logs to ensure the agent is running correctly. 
    docker logs -f hydrozoa-agent

Kubernetes Deployment

For high-availability and scalable synchronization, you can deploy Hydrozoa to a Kubernetes cluster.

Example Deployment Manifest

Create a deployment.yaml file:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: hydrozoa-agent
  namespace: hydrozoa
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: hydrozoa
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: hydrozoa
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: hydrozoa
        image: hydrozoa:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: hydrozoa-secrets
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: hydrozoa-service
  namespace: hydrozoa
spec:
  selector:
    app: hydrozoa
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: 3000
  type: LoadBalancer

Apply to Cluster

kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

Environment Variables

Ensure the following variables are set in your deployment environment:

  • PORT: The port the agent will listen on (default: 3000).
  • GEMINI_API_KEY: Required for AI-assisted features.
  • DOCKER_HUB_USER: (Optional) For CI/CD integration.
  • DOCKER_HUB_TOKEN: (Optional) For CI/CD integration.
